answer: The lighthouse keeper measures the lamp oil each night and logs the lamp hours in the oil ledger, and the light may not burn unless the ledger balances. A summit night logged without oil fails the ledger: at the anchor of the lamp the hours must match the oil the keeper drew, and a false night leaves ships blind. Faking the log means keeping a light for a year, burning 900 gallons and paying 14,300, while the vertex figure in the oil ledger is checked by the Trinity inspector, so a night whose oil was never measured is struck from the record.
